meta.title: Ch 4: Security Analysis — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 4 (Security Analysis).

questions.q: A levered equity beta of 1.35, D/E of 0.5 and tax rate 30%; the unlevered (asset) beta per Hamada is:
questions.why: βU = βL ÷ [1 + (1−t)×D/E] = 1.35 ÷ (1 + 0.7×0.5) = 1.35/1.35 = 1.00. A 0.90 answer forgets the tax shield (dividing by 1+D/E); 1.82 multiplies instead of divides, 1.82 multiplies instead of divides, 1.35 is the raw levered beta.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the lever/unlever pair is CAPM's arithmetic heart Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Untwist the gearing: divide by (1 + after-tax D/E) to find pure business risk; multiply to add gearing back.

questions.q: A portfolio with equal weights in two stocks (β 0.8 and 1.6) has beta:
questions.why: Portfolio beta = weighted average of individual betas = (0.8+1.6)/2 = 1.2 — no diversification math needed for beta itself.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — linearity of beta is a freebie that trips 'correlation' distractors AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Betans average; variances covary. Don't mix the two ledgers.

questions.q: A stock with β 1.2, actual return 13%, rf 5%, market return 9%; Jensen's alpha:
questions.why: CAPM-required return = 5 + 1.2×(9−5) = 9.8%; α = 13 − 9.8 = +3.2% — positive alpha says the stock outperformed what its beta required. The −3.2 sign flip is the classic trap.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — α arithmetic with sign traps AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Alpha = the surprise the market never charged you for: return minus what beta required.

questions.q: For an Indian equity, which is a component of SYSTEMATIC risk?
o: RBI repo decision and oil shocks
questions.why: Macroeconomy-wide factors (rates, FX, oil, policy) hit all; firm-specific events are diversifiable.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — factor-classification quick sets AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: If the news moves the whole market, you own it forever.

questions.q: If semi-strong EMH holds, which strategy still earns abnormal returns?
questions.why: Semi-strong: prices reflect all public info ⇒ technical AND fundamental analysis fail; only non-public info (strong form violation) can beat it.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the three-form ladder with what beats what AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Semi-strong means the library won't help; only the diary will.

questions.q: Stock bought at 400, dividend 10 received mid-year, sold at 430. Holding-period return:
questions.why: HPR = (P1 − P0 + D)/P0 = (30+10)/400 = 10% — the classic slip is quoting 7.5%, the price gain alone.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — price gain + income, all over entry Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: The sale tells half the story; the dividend tells the rest.

questions.q: Nominal return 12%, inflation 6%; the real return is closest to:
questions.why: Fisher: (1.12/1.06) − 1 = 5.66%; the 12−6=6 subtraction is the approximation examiners set as the trap on precise marks.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — divide the relatives, don't subtract the labels Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Inflation is the toll booth between earning and owning.

questions.q: The historical equity risk premium over risk-free rate is used in CAPM; its long-run behaviour across mature markets is roughly:
o: Historically around 3-8% per year and time-varying
questions.why: Documented long-run studies (e.g., global returns datasets) put the real equity premium in the mid-single digits annually with wide period sensitivity — hence the exam loves the caveat: premium is an estimate, sensitive to window and geography; ICAI accepts the stated assumption whichever the question gives.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — estimate, not constant — say so in the assumption note AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A century of averages hides every decade's surprise.

questions.q: Returns with negative skew and excess kurtosis imply the normal distribution:
questions.why: Negative skew = heavier left tail than normal; fat kurtosis = both tails heavier — normal-based risk metrics then understate crash risk; this is the documented case for t-distributions and EVT in stress work.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — normal curve trims the tails — the tails are where you live Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The bell curve has no memory of 2008.
